title: Saved drives contract
description: Language-neutral saved-drive shapes shared by iOS, Android, backend, and admin. ride mirrors the Firestore `rides/{rideId}` document (docs/firebase-data-model.md). Stats are computed server-side by drives.save from the submitted recording; the full route GPS track lives only in Cloud Storage under the member-gated rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/ prefix, with one bounded exception — routeThumbnail, a ~64-point simplified overview of the route stored on the document so the History list can draw a drive's shape without a second read. maxSpeedMetersPerSecond IS stored (an explicit 2026-07 product decision reversing the earlier 'no top-speed field exists anywhere' rule); it is a neutral stat shown beside distance and duration and must never be turned into a record, ranking or achievement. Drives saved before that decision carry neither field and are not backfilled; clients render their missing-value placeholder. Firestore stores timestamps as native Timestamp values; this contract describes their ISO 8601 JSON serialization.

ride.description: Firestore `rides/{rideId}`. Owner-only read (membership not required — drives saved during a previous membership stay listable); all writes go through drives.save / drives.delete.

distanceMeters.description: Server-computed; null for summary-only saves (no route points).

maxSpeedMetersPerSecond.description: Highest plausible instantaneous speed over the submitted points, server-computed with the same >200 km/h GPS-glitch filter distance uses; null for summary-only saves. ABSENT (not null) on drives saved before 2026-07, which are not backfilled — read it as 'unknown' and render a missing-value placeholder, never 0. A neutral factual stat displayed at the same weight as distance and duration: never a record, personal best, ranking or comparison between drives.

routeThumbnail.description: The drive's route simplified to at most 64 points (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker, so corners survive) as an encoded polyline at 1e5 precision — a few hundred bytes. Lets the History list draw the drive's shape with no extra read and no map instance; the full track stays in Cloud Storage. Null when there is no drawable shape (fewer than two points, or a stationary recording), and ABSENT on drives saved before 2026-07 — both render the list's placeholder.

routePath.description: Canonical Cloud Storage path (rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/route.bin); the file itself is member-gated.

previewImagePath.description: Canonical Cloud Storage path (rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/preview.png); member-gated like the route.

sourceSessionId.description: Client recording identifier used for idempotent save retries.

vehicleId.description: The garage car this drive was driven in (the one chosen in the 'Start driving' picker), or null. Not backfilled onto drives saved before the field existed.

carImagePath.description: Denormalized cover-photo Storage path of the driven car, so the History card renders a round photo without a vehicle read. Null when no car was recorded.

convoyMembers.description: The OTHER members of the convoy this drive was part of, denormalized so the History card can show who you drove with. Empty array on a solo drive; ABSENT on drives saved before the field existed (not backfilled) and on the server-side convoy finalize baseline.

ride.comment: maxSpeedMetersPerSecond, routeThumbnail, vehicleId, carImagePath and convoyMembers are deliberately NOT required: drives.save writes them, but drives saved before each field existed are not backfilled and simply lack the keys. Requiring them would describe a shape the collection does not have.

convoyMember.description: One OTHER member of the convoy a drive was part of, denormalized onto the ride (and submitted on the save) so the History card can show who you drove with without an extra read. Mirrors the backend zod (functions/src/drives/drives-core.ts convoyMembers) and the Android ConvoyDriveMembers wire shape.

driveHistoryItem.description: Allowlisted saved-drive metadata returned by drives.listHistory. Internal ownership, Storage-path, source-session and full-route fields are deliberately absent.

listDriveHistoryRequest.description: Optional cursor and bounded page size for drives.listHistory. Community never receives a continuation cursor.

listDriveHistoryResponse.description: Server-authoritative history page. Tier and time-window decisions are resolved from backend state and server time, never client claims or device time.

driveStatsRequest.description: Optional local-calendar-month window for the 'this month' fields of drives.stats. monthStartMillis and monthEndMillis are Unix-epoch millisecond integers and must be supplied together (or both omitted). The backend validates them against server time: the range must straddle server now, span a single calendar month (27-32 days), and be bounded near the present; device time is never trusted.

driveStatsResponse.description: Server-authoritative statistics aggregate from drives.stats, computed over ONLY the caller's tier-visible drives (the same subscription policy as drives.listHistory: Community = newest 5, Plus = rolling 90 days, Supporter = everything), so deeper stats are a paid benefit and the aggregate never widens access to hidden history. All distances are metres and speeds metres/second. A maximum figure (longest/fastest/highestMax) is 0 when no visible drive carries that stat, never a false negative. thisMonthDrives/thisMonthDistanceMeters are 0 when no month range was supplied. tier and serverNowMillis let the client label the scope without trusting device time.

averageDriveMeters.description: Mean distance per tier-visible drive (totalDistanceMeters / totalDrives); summary-only saves with a null distance still count toward the denominator. 0 when there are no visible drives.

driveLifetimeStatsResponse.description: TRUE-LIFETIME statistics aggregate from drives.lifetimeStats, computed over ALL of the caller's drives regardless of subscription tier — the deliberately UN-PAYWALLED counterpart to driveStatsResponse (which is tier-scoped). There is no tier field and no thisMonth* fields: lifetime achievement (profile 'my stats', the Vägfarare lifetime-distance badge) must not shrink on a downgrade, and this aggregate has no month window. All distances are metres and speeds metres/second. totalDrives is a Firestore count() over the owner's rides (the true ride-document count); a drive with a malformed durationSeconds is dropped from the sums but still counts toward totalDrives, so totalDrives may exceed the number of summed drives when data is corrupt. averageDriveMeters is totalDistanceMeters / totalDrives (0 when no drives); summary-only saves with a null distance still count toward the denominator. A maximum figure (longest/fastest/highestMax) is 0 when no drive carries that stat, never a false negative. serverNowMillis lets the client label the scope without trusting device time.

deletableDriveItem.description: One row of the owner-only deletion inventory returned by drives.listDeletable. Deliberately carries ONLY what a 'delete this drive' list needs — id, when it happened, and its label. No distance, speed, duration, route path/thumbnail, image or source-session field is included.

listDeletableDrivesRequest.description: Optional cursor and bounded page size for drives.listDeletable.

listDeletableDrivesResponse.description: Owner-only deletion inventory page. Returns ALL the caller's owned drives regardless of tier window (unlike drives.listHistory), so a downgraded user can still delete drives the tier window now hides.

routePoint.description: A single recorded GPS point submitted to drives.save. Points must be ordered by timestampMs.

saveDriveRequest.description: Input for drives.save (member-only). Distance/duration/average speed/maximum speed and the route thumbnail are all computed server-side from routePoints; implausible GPS jumps (>200 km/h implied speed) are excluded from both distance and maximum speed.

vehicleId.description: Firestore-safe id of the garage car this drive was driven in. Mirrors the backend zod: character class excludes '/', and the leading lookahead rejects the reserved '.' and '..' ids.

carImagePath.description: Cover-photo Storage path of the driven car, denormalized onto the ride for the History card.

convoyMembers.description: The OTHER members of the convoy this drive was part of (uid + optional display name + optional avatar path), submitted so the ride records who you drove with. Optional and omitted on a solo drive or by older clients; the backend de-duplicates by uid and caps the array at 24.

saveDriveResponse.description: Result of drives.save, including the canonical Cloud Storage paths the client uploads the route file and preview image to. routeThumbnail is stored on the ride document but deliberately not echoed here — it is derived from points the caller just sent.

alreadySaved.description: True when an idempotent retry returned the existing drive.

deleteDriveRequest.description: Input for drives.delete (any active owner; membership not required).

rideId.description: Firestore-safe document ID — no path separators.

routeUrlRequest.description: Input for drives.routeUrl (owner-only, tier-gated). Names the drive whose full GPS route file a signed download URL is requested for.

rideId.description: Firestore-safe document ID — no path separators.

routeUrlResponse.description: Result of drives.routeUrl: a short-lived (5 min) V4 signed URL for the drive's route.bin, and the epoch-millis instant it expires. The client should download promptly and never persist the URL. permission-denied when the drive is outside the caller's subscription-tier history window; not-found for a missing or non-owned drive; failed-precondition when there is no stored route file or when V4 signing is unavailable.

url.description: Short-lived V4 signed read URL for rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/route.bin.

expiresAtMillis.description: Unix epoch milliseconds at which the signed URL expires (~5 minutes after issue).
